content.value_statement: Technical teams often need consistent documentation for APIs, data models, integrations, security, and infrastructure. This skill provides templates and checklists that turn source evidence into structured technical requirements.
actual_capabilities: Documents REST endpoints with request, response, authentication, and business rule sections.
Guides GraphQL, event, and message API analysis with reusable schema templates.
Captures entities, relationships, constraints, indexes, and data flows.
Structures integration documentation for protocols, authentication, data exchange, errors, SLAs, and monitoring.
Documents authentication, authorization, data protection, compliance, and infrastructure requirements.
Summarizes API contracts, data models, integrations, security, infrastructure, and technical debt.
limitations: It provides analysis templates and checklists, not automated vulnerability testing.
It depends on readable source files, documentation, or architecture evidence.
It does not execute commands or call external services.
It may leave placeholders when the repository lacks enough detail.

use_cases.title: Create API Requirement Notes
use_cases.description: Turn existing routes, controllers, or OpenAPI files into clear endpoint documentation.

use_cases.title: Map Integration Contracts
use_cases.description: Document external systems, protocols, authentication, data exchange, error handling, and monitoring needs.

use_cases.title: Prepare Security Requirements
use_cases.description: Capture authentication, authorization, data protection, compliance, and audit requirements for a system review.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Technical Surface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project and summarize its APIs, data models, integrations, security areas, and infrastructure. Cite the files you used.

prompt_templates.title: Document API Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the REST and GraphQL interfaces. Produce endpoint notes with authentication, request fields, response shapes, errors, and business rules.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Integrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Find integration points and document direction, protocol, data exchange, authentication, retries, monitoring, and SLA assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Full Technical Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete technical analysis covering APIs, data models, integrations, security controls, infrastructure, technical debt, and open questions.

output_examples.output: A structured endpoint summary with purpose, authentication, request fields, response outcomes, errors, and related business rules.

output_examples.input: Review integration patterns for order fulfillment.
output_examples.output: A comparison of synchronous, asynchronous, file-based, and data integration options with requirements and tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Document security requirements for customer data.
output_examples.output: A requirements summary for authentication, roles, sensitive data handling, encryption, masking, compliance, and audit evidence.

best_practices: Start with existing source files and cite evidence for each requirement.
Separate confirmed facts from assumptions and open questions.
Use the templates consistently across APIs, data, integrations, security, and infrastructure.
anti_patterns: Do not invent system behavior when evidence is missing.
Do not mix business requirements with implementation guesses.
Do not treat template examples as production configuration.

faq.question: What does this skill help document?
faq.answer: It helps document APIs, data models, integrations, security requirements, infrastructure, and technical debt.

faq.question: Does it run code or commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is limited to reading, searching, globbing, and language server inspection.

faq.question: Can it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It organizes security requirements but does not perform penetration testing or vulnerability scanning.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Source files, API specifications, database schemas, architecture notes, and existing requirement documents work best.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should missing information be handled?
faq.answer: Mark it as an assumption or open question instead of filling the template with unsupported details.
